nodes.summary:
For finite measures $\mu$ and $
u$ on a measurable space, the total variation distances satisfy $d_{TV}(\mu, 
u) = d_{TV}(
u, \mu)$.
nodes.title: Symmetry of total variation distance

nodes.summary: Let $\Omega$ be a measurable space in which every singleton is measurable, and let $a, b \in \Omega$. The total variation distance between the Dirac measures $\delta_a$ and $\delta_b$ is $0$ if $a = b$ and $1$ if $a \neq b$.
nodes.title: Total variation distance between Dirac measures

nodes.summary:
For finite measures $\mu$ and $
u$ on a measurable space, the total variation distance $d_{TV}(\mu, 
u)$ is $0$ if and only if $\mu = 
u$.
nodes.title: Total variation distance vanishes only for equal measures

nodes.summary: For probability measures $\mu$ and $\nu$ on a measurable space, the total variation distance satisfies $d_{TV}(\mu, \nu) \le 1$.
nodes.title: Total variation distance between probability measures is at most one

nodes.summary: For finite measures $\mu$ and $\nu$ on a measurable space, the total variation distance satisfies $0 \le d_{TV}(\mu, \nu)$.
nodes.title: Total variation distance is nonnegative

nodes.summary: For every finite measure $\mu$ on a measurable space, the total variation distance $d_{TV}(\mu, \mu)$ is $0$.
nodes.title: Total variation distance from a measure to itself

nodes.summary:
For finite measures $\mu$, $
u$ and $ho$ on a measurable space, the total variation distance satisfies $d_{TV}(\mu, ho) \le d_{TV}(\mu, 
u) + d_{TV}(
u, ho)$.
nodes.title: Triangle inequality for total variation distance

nodes.summary:
For finite measures $\mu$ and $
u$ on a measurable space $\Omega$, the total variation distance $d_{TV}(\mu, 
u)$ is the real number $\sup_B |\mu(B) - 
u(B)|$, where the supremum runs over all measurable sets $B \subseteq \Omega$ and the masses $\mu(B)$ and $
u(B)$ are taken as real numbers.
nodes.title: Total variation distance between finite measures

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
